messages:
customer_cox: Hey @maria_support — we're getting a bunch of 429s this morning across our service. Happens when our worker fleet does a short burst (~120 requests/sec) for ~10s. We use 3 API keys and route through two proxy IPs.

maria_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a sample request ID or response body? Are you sending the same API key across both IPs or different keys?

customer_cox: Here's one response: `\{"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\", \"message\":\"Rate limit exceeded\", \"hint\":\"scope=project\"\}`. Request ID: r-0a1b2c3d. We distribute evenly across 3 keys; each backend worker picks a key at random. IPs are 34.210.1.12 and 34.210.1.13. No other services hitting that org.

maria_support: Thanks. That "hint": "scope=project" is interesting — it suggests the project quota was hit, not the org-level. Are you on any dedicated capacity or on hosted API?

customer_cox: Hosted API standard plan. We thought keys had their own per-key bursts, not pooled to the project. Is that not the case?

alex_sre: Quick heads-up: for hosted plans we enforce limits in this order: per-key -> per-IP (if IP-scoped quotas exist) -> project -> org. But there are edge cases when a request comes in with multiple auth headers (proxy rewriting) where we de-duplicate and attribute to a project. Could be happening here.

sam_engineer: Jumping in — can you run a repro with curl that includes the API key and the forwarding IP so we can see the headers? Also want the raw response headers (X-RateLimit-*) if present.

customer_cox: Repro curl attached: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ABC123" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 34.210.1.12" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate``` Response headers I saw: `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Scope: project`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 12`. Body same as above.

maria_support: Good data. Two hypotheses: (1) your per-key rate is actually low and random distribution still tripped project because other keys have lower remaining; (2) proxy is collapsing keys into one project identity (we've seen proxies rewriting auth to a proxy-managed token). Do you have any logs showing which key the worker used for that request-id?

customer_cox: Our app logs the key id at the worker: `key_id=sk-prod-ABC123` for r-0a1b2c3d. We rotate keys per process.

sam_engineer: Can you run a quick spike where you pin a single worker to one key and send 150 req/s for 20s from a single IP? We need to check whether per-key limits alone trigger 429 or if the project pool trips.

customer_cox: Doing that now... will post results.

(30s pause)

customer_cox: Repro: pinned key to sk-prod-ABC123, single IP 34.210.1.12, 150 req/s for 20s. After 8s we start seeing 429s and X-RateLimit-Scope: project. Each response shows Remaining=0.

alex_sre: Excellent repro — confirms project-level limit is being enforced before per-key exhaustion. That is unexpected based on our intended ordering. Opening a short investigation. @sam_engineer can you look at the quota-check ordering code path?

sam_engineer: On it. Quick grep shows we recently refactored the auth middleware; there was a change to merge request provenance earlier in the pipeline (to compute usage attribution). Possible bug: when provenance merge fails it sets a fallback owner to the project's default, causing per-key checks to be skipped.

maria_support: Customer-facing note: this means in some proxy/fanout setups your per-key bursts may not be honored, and limits may fall back to project. We're escalating.

customer_cox: Oof — that's rough. Any ETA or workaround? We can throttle ourselves but would prefer to keep burst behavior.

sam_engineer: Short-term workaround: add a header `X-Client-Key-Id: sk-prod-ABC123` to assert explicit key id (we'll honor that header in auth if signed by the same key). We can also whitelist your project for higher project burst while we fix.

maria_support: @customer_cox I can apply a temporary project burst increase (10k/sec for 1 hour) if you want to avoid interruptions while engineering patches. Want me to do that?

customer_cox: Please do the temp increase, thanks. We'll also add the X-Client-Key-Id header.

sam_engineer: Patch plan: revert the refactor that changed provenance merge ordering and add unit tests for proxy-forwarded auth (X-Forwarded-For + forwarded auth headers). I can have a patch in the staging branch in ~2h and a limited deploy to canary the next window.

alex_sre: Also adding a runtime guard: if provenance resolution returns ambiguous, we fall back to per-key checks rather than project default. Safer for customers.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued by sam_engineer: revert/provenance-ordering — staging build 2026-03-15_09_45 (canary 10%).

maria_support: Customer, I applied the temporary burst quota increase at 1968754380 (one-time for 60 minutes). Can you confirm whether errors stop?

customer_cox: After change + header we haven't seen 429s for the last 30s. Thanks!

sam_engineer: I'll run the unit + integration tests now and leave the canary running for 30m. If metrics look good, we'll roll to prod.

alex_sre: Follow-ups: (1) add explicit docs about scoping precedence (per-key -> per-IP -> project -> org) and known proxy caveats, (2) add monitoring alert when X-RateLimit-Scope is project but request includes explicit key header, (3) schedule audit of other refactors touching auth pipeline.

maria_support: Noted. @customer_cox — I'll leave the thread open while canary runs. Ping us if anything pops up. :thumbsup:

customer_cox: Will do. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

quota-bot: Notice: Project quota bump applied to project-id: proj-87x at 1968754380 by maria_support. Expires in 3600s.

deploy-bot: Canary started: revert/provenance-ordering -> 10% traffic at 1968754390.

maria_support: Closing loop for now but will update when deploy is fully rolled.

customer_cox: Thanks all!"
